svg.text: IMU test board · ICM-45686, LSM6DSV320X, ASM330LHH and ADXL375 on one rigid PCB
AI MotoLogger · Rev 0 · 2026-11-08 · number next to a pin = chip pin number · net labels match the KiCad schematic · 0603 passives · all parts on the top side
Goal: choose the IMU for the main logger from bench tests and rides on a Yamaha YZ 125 test bike · are ±32 g enough? how hot does the board get? · hand-assembled with a stencil
A · J1: 1×15 HEADER, 2.54 MM · DUPONT ON THE BENCH, CABLE ON THE BIKE
GND between SCK and MOSI, and after MISO:
each fast signal has its return next to it.
Bench: male header and Dupont wires
Bike: no Dupont wires. A second board,
without the header: the cable is soldered
into the J1 holes and held by a cable tie
through two holes next to J1
B · POWER: 5 V FROM THE NUCLEO → FERRITE BEAD → DEDICATED 3.3 V LDO (THE IMUs DON'T SHARE THE MCU'S RAIL)
U1: 200 mA, input ≤ 6 V, stable with low-ESR
ceramic capacitors. The whole board draws < 10 mA.
C · SHARED SPI BUS: ONE OR GATE IN FRONT OF EACH IMU's SDI · PULL-UP ON EVERY CS · 33 Ω ON MISO
Y = MOSI OR CS: while its CS is high, an IMU's SDI stays at 1, so traffic meant for another IMU can't look like an I²C start to it (ADXL375 Rev. B, Fig. 24 and
“Preventing Bus Traffic Errors”). The ADXL375 can't turn off its I²C interface, and the ICM-45686 datasheet doesn't say how. The ST parts can (IF_CFG / CTRL4_C): firmware does it too.
D · THE FOUR IMUs: DECOUPLING AS EACH DATASHEET ASKS, RIGHT AT THE PIN
· SPI mode 3 for all four (the ADXL375 requires it; ST and TDK support it).
Clock limits: ADXL375 2–5 MHz (≥ 2 MHz for 1600 and 3200 Hz) · ST ≤ 10 MHz · ICM ≤ 24 MHz.
All at 5 MHz: ~115 KB/s of data = ~20 % of the bus.
· At start-up: I2C_I3C_disable = 1 (U3, IF_CFG 03h) · I2C_disable = 1 (U4, CTRL4_C 13h) ·
turn off the internal pull-up on AP_SDO in U2 (Table 10).
· The ADXL375 comes from AliExpress, and its DEVID (0xE5) is the same as the ADXL345's.
At rest, 1 g ≈ 20 LSB (49 mg/LSB); ~256 LSB means a relabelled ADXL345.
· INT_* to TIM2 CH1–CH4 (32-bit input capture): a time stamp for every FIFO batch (block G).
· Axes: each IMU is rotated on the PCB so that X, Y and Z match (U5 at −90°),
and the axes are marked on the silkscreen (ICM §11.1, ST Fig. 1, ADXL Fig. 3).
· ADXL375 VS: if it needs filtering, use a ferrite bead in place of R3, not a resistor (VS ≥ VDD_IO).
· Soldering (TN0018 §3.3–3.4): 0.12 mm steel stencil, apertures at 70–90 % of the pad;
no solder on the sides of the LGA packages; cool down at ≤ 3 °C/s.
1. All four respond: WHO_AM_I / DEVID, plus the relabelled-ADXL345 check.
2. Noise at rest of each one against its datasheet (density, offset, drift with temperature).
3. Rubber-mallet hits: the ICM (±32 g) cross-checks the LSM6DSV320X high-g channel
between 16 and 32 g; the ADXL375 (±200 g) covers everything above.
4. Real peaks: do they go past 16 g? Past 32 g? Does any sensor saturate?
5. Engine vibration: spectrum from each sensor and gyro drift under vibration
(rectification). TDK advertises vibration rejection; ST gives no figure.
6. Board temperature, from the internal sensor of all four.
7. Timing: FIFO batches time-stamped by INT against the MCU counter.
The result decides: LSM6DSV320X alone, ICM-45686 alone, or one of them + ADXL375.
G · J1 → NUCLEO-U5A5ZJ-Q THROUGH THE ZIO CONNECTORS (UM2861 TABLES 15, 16, 18) · MORPHO HEADERS NOT FITTED
SPI1_SCK · LD1 is on PC7 by default (SB21)
TIM2_CH1 · SB60 ON by default (not the button)
TIM2_CH2 (DS13543) · uses up analog input A8
TIM2_CH3 · also on CN10-15: leave it free
TIM2 is 32-bit: the four INTs are time-stamped by input capture, with no interrupt latency. The GNSS PPS goes to TIM5
(also 32-bit), started together with TIM2. Still free: SDMMC1 (CN8), USART2 (CN9), FDCAN1 (PD0/PD1), A0–A5.
H · BOARD LAYOUT FOR THE IMUs (ST TN0018 REV 8)
· 54 × 50 mm, 1.6 mm, 4 layers: signals / GND / +3.3 V / signals.
All parts on the top side.
· Under each IMU: no tracks, vias or copper pour on the top layer (§3.2, §3.9),
and pour keep-out areas on all four layers.
· The four IMUs sit in a row in the middle of the board, between the four
M3 mounting holes, more than 8 mm from each hole (§3.2, §6.2, §6.3).
· J1 is more than 20 mm from the IMUs, because the cable pulls there (§6.5).
Two Ø3 mm holes next to J1 take the cable tie.
· The LDO (U1) is more than 9 mm from the IMUs: heat (§6.4).
· Solder paste on the LGA pads reduced by a custom DRC rule (−0.025 mm
per side): 79 % of the pad on the 2.5 × 3 mm parts, 87 % on the ADXL375.
· Pads: footprint pad = LGA pad + 0.1 mm; solder mask 0.1 mm larger,
not fitted on the bike board
· Schematic captured in KiCad 10: the netlist
· 4-layer PCB routed by hand; DRC 0 errors.
· PCB and stencil sponsored by PCBWay,
· Next: hand assembly with the stencil, bench
tests on the Nucleo, then the bike.
AI MotoLogger is a data logger for a KTM 250 SX-F
suspension, brakes, wheel speeds, ECU (CAN, listen-
only) and wideband lambda, all on GNSS time.
AI MotoLogger · IMU test board for bench and bike tests · not the final logger board
